title: Hugging Face Dataset Types — Catalog & Project-Fit Report
generated_for: Orchestrated system of fine-tuned specialist LLMs — Phase A 'Knowledge Searcher': 28 text reasoning/knowledge specialists (10 core + 18 applied verticals) grounded in 84 dense, gated knowledge bases (1,754 nodes / 3,273 edges / 1,157 competency-questions), with a router on top. Fit is judged for FINE-TUNING and EVALUATING these text specialists, not for pretraining a base model from scratch.
rating_scale: 1–5 stars = fit for FINE-TUNING/EVALUATING our 28 text specialists (5 best). Tier S/A/B/C/D derived from the rating.

legend.♥: live like-count observed on the Hub during this session
legend.maps_to: specialist codes the type most directly serves

axes.functional (training purpose): the primary axis used below — how the data is USED to build a specialist

types.what_it_is: Single-turn (instruction, optional input) → ideal-response pairs. The canonical supervised fine-tuning format that teaches a base model to follow directions and adopt a behavior/persona.
types.where_useful: The backbone format for turning each of our 28 specialists into an obedient, on-domain responder. Our specialist specs (role / decision_procedure / workflow / escalation_triggers) convert almost 1:1 into instruction→response exemplars.
types.edge_over_others: Cheapest, most direct lever on behavior: a few thousand high-quality pairs reshape tone, format, and scope without RL machinery. Easiest type to synthesize from our own KBs.
maps_to_specialists: ALL — base behavior layer for every specialist
types.rationale: Primary vehicle for specialist behavior. Directly generable from our specs + KBs; nothing else gives faster control over how a specialist answers.

types.what_it_is: Problems paired with explicit step-by-step solution traces (often distilled from a strong 'thinking' model), so the student learns the derivation, not just the final answer.
types.where_useful: Teaches the multi-step grounded reasoning our specialists' decision_procedures and dominance_rules encode. Highest-leverage type for the core reasoning specialists.
types.edge_over_others: Transfers *process*, not just outputs — the only type that reliably lifts multi-hop / show-your-work performance. Pairs naturally with our competency-questions as prompts and our KB edges as the reasoning skeleton.
types.rationale: Most directly encodes the reasoning behavior the project exists to produce. Our edge/dominance structure is a natural scaffold for generating traces.

types.what_it_is: Question → answer, in extractive, open-book (context-grounded/RAG), closed-book, or multiple-choice form.
types.where_useful: Train and *evaluate* specialists directly against their competency-questions; grounded QA teaches answer-from-context discipline that mirrors our KB-grounded answering and citation requirement.
types.edge_over_others: Only type whose schema matches our 1,157 competency-questions 1:1 — both a training format and the native evaluation harness. Multiple-choice (MMLU-style) gives cheap, automatic scoring.
types.rationale: Doubles as training data and as the validation harness for competency-question coverage. Grounded-QA discipline = our core anti-hallucination requirement.

types.what_it_is: Text or instruction data concentrated in one vertical (medicine, law, finance, security, etc.) — for continued pretraining or domain SFT.
types.where_useful: Feeds the 18 applied verticals (security, health, uslaw, markets, money, business, maker, design…). Injects domain vocabulary, conventions, and edge-cases our distilled KBs reference but don't fully contain.
types.edge_over_others: Highest factual density per token for a given specialist; closes the gap between a KB's compressed nodes and the specialist's need for broad in-domain fluency. Filterable by HF `language`/domain tags.
types.rationale: Direct nutrient for the applied half of the roster. Must be vetted against our baked-in boundaries (defensive-only / informational-not-clinical / not-advice).

types.what_it_is: Entities + typed relations (triples / node-edge graphs), ontologies, and structured relational records — sometimes verbalized into text.
types.where_useful: Our 84 KBs *are* this shape (nodes/edges/conflict_axes/dominance_rules). Graph datasets train KB construction, completion, consistency-checking, and node/edge verbalization for the kr & worldmodel specialists.
types.edge_over_others: Structurally identical to our own data — uniquely supports KB self-extension and validation (the 35/35 dense gate). No other type teaches relation/dominance reasoning natively.
types.rationale: Mirrors the project's native data structure; the path to making specialists able to grow and audit their own KBs.

types.what_it_is: A prompt with a preferred vs. rejected response (or scalar reward), used for DPO/RLHF/reward-model training.
types.where_useful: Calibrates *quality and boundaries* after SFT: prefer grounded/cited answers over confident guesses, prefer correct refusals/escalations on out-of-scope or unsafe asks. Directly enforces our escalation_triggers.
types.edge_over_others: Only type that teaches relative judgement and graceful refusal — SFT alone can't express 'this answer is better' or 'decline this'. Critical for the security/health/uslaw boundary behavior.
types.rationale: The alignment/boundary lever. High value but needs SFT first; pairs can be synthesized (good = KB-grounded, bad = ungrounded).

types.what_it_is: Full multi-turn conversations with system/user/assistant roles and context carryover.
types.where_useful: Teaches specialists to hold context, ask clarifying questions before answering, and behave well inside the router→specialist handoff (a conversation, not a one-shot).
types.edge_over_others: Only type that trains state-tracking and clarification — exactly the behavior a router-fronted specialist needs when a query is under-specified.
types.rationale: Makes specialists usable in dialogue and improves the orchestration handoff; one tier below single-turn SFT for our mostly-retrieval workload.

types.what_it_is: Query↔passage pairs (often with hard negatives) for training embedders, retrievers, and rerankers.
types.where_useful: Powers two project organs: (1) the ROUTER that picks the right specialist, and (2) KB grounding / RAG that fetches the right nodes before answering.
types.edge_over_others: The retrieval backbone — without good embeddings, routing and grounding degrade no matter how good the specialists are. Independent of generation, so it's reusable across the whole fleet.
types.rationale: Infrastructure for routing + grounding. High value, but serves the plumbing rather than a specialist's voice.

types.what_it_is: Model-generated instruction/preference/reasoning data, often persona- or seed-driven and filtered for quality.
types.where_useful: Our fastest path to *bespoke* per-specialist data: seed a generator with each KB's nodes/competency-questions to mint on-domain SFT, preference, and trace data at scale.
types.edge_over_others: Scales to all 28 specialists without human labeling and stays perfectly on-schema with our KBs. Quality is controllable via the same dense gate we already enforce.
types.rationale: Force-multiplier given we already own 84 dense, gated KBs as seeds. Risk: model-collapse/contamination if unfiltered — reuse our validation gate.

types.what_it_is: Curated, often held-out test sets with official metrics (knowledge, reasoning, retrieval, code, safety).
types.where_useful: Measures whether a fine-tune actually helped, per specialist and per domain. Maps onto our competency-question coverage and the routing accuracy of the orchestrator.
types.edge_over_others: The only type whose purpose is measurement — guards against regressions and overfitting to synthetic data. Standardized scoring makes specialist-vs-specialist comparison meaningful.
types.rationale: Not training fuel, but essential to prove the project works; aligns with the 35/35 gate philosophy already in the repo.

types.what_it_is: Harmful/adversarial prompts paired with safe responses or refusals; jailbreak and toxicity probes.
types.where_useful: Hardens the boundaries already baked into our specs: security = offense-aware DEFENSE only; health/psych = informational, not clinical; uslaw = literacy, not advice; markets/money/business = education, not advice.
types.edge_over_others: Only type that explicitly trains *refusal and escalation under adversarial pressure* — directly operationalizes our escalation_triggers and conflicts_and_dominance rules.
types.rationale: Protects the project's stated guardrails; pairs with preference data. High importance precisely for the risk-bearing verticals.

types.what_it_is: Math problems with worked solutions / final answers (arithmetic → competition level).
types.where_useful: Sharpens the quantitative specialists and provides verifiable rewards (answer-checkable) for RL-style training.
types.edge_over_others: Automatically gradable — rare, valuable signal for self-improvement loops. Strong reasoning transfer to adjacent analytic specialists.
types.rationale: High value for two specialists, narrow for the other 26; verifiability is the differentiator.

types.what_it_is: Source code, code-instruction pairs, and repo-level bug-fix tasks.
types.where_useful: Feeds the developer/AI-compute specialists and any tool-emitting behavior; SWE-style tasks evaluate agentic repair.
types.edge_over_others: Execution-verifiable (tests pass / fail) — like math, gives a hard reward signal. Underpins any future tool-using orchestration.
types.rationale: Strong for the engineering verticals, peripheral to the knowledge-finding core.

types.what_it_is: Prompts → structured tool/API calls, and multi-step agent trajectories (plan→act→observe).
types.where_useful: Trains the orchestration layer: how the router and specialists emit calls, hand off, and chain steps — the 'loops' specialist's home turf.
types.edge_over_others: Only type that teaches *structured action emission* and tool selection — the skill the whole orchestrated system depends on at runtime.
types.rationale: Important for Phase-B orchestration; less so for Phase-A single-specialist answering. Will rise in priority as the system becomes agentic.

types.what_it_is: Premise→hypothesis entailment, claim↔evidence verification, and stance/argument structure labels.
types.where_useful: Trains the argue & evsynth specialists to weigh evidence, detect contradiction, and respect our conflict_axes / dominance_rules.
types.edge_over_others: Directly teaches contradiction/entailment detection — the mechanic behind our conflict-resolution and anti-rework rules; rare elsewhere.
types.rationale: Specialized but squarely aligned with the evidence-synthesis core; moderate breadth.

types.what_it_is: Text → label (sentiment, topic, intent, acceptability, etc.).
types.where_useful: Auxiliary signal for routing/intent detection and content filtering; lightweight guardrails.
types.edge_over_others: Cheap, fast, high-accuracy for narrow decisions — but produces labels, not the grounded explanations our specialists owe.
types.rationale: Useful plumbing, but our value proposition is explanation + grounding, which classification doesn't teach.

types.what_it_is: Per-token labels: entities, parts of speech, spans.
types.where_useful: Entity extraction to populate/link KB nodes and to power retrieval filters; supports the linguistics specialist.
types.edge_over_others: Best precision for structured extraction feeding KB construction — but a narrow preprocessing role, not a reasoning skill.
types.rationale: Helpful for KB ingestion pipelines; marginal for specialist behavior itself.

types.what_it_is: Long document → condensed summary (abstractive or extractive).
types.where_useful: Supports evidence-synthesis, bibliographic, and scholarly-comms specialists; useful for compressing sources into KB nodes.
types.edge_over_others: Teaches faithful compression — adjacent to our KB-distillation process — but risks unsupported abstraction if not grounded.
types.rationale: Relevant to a few specialists and to KB authoring; not a core reasoning capability.

types.what_it_is: Aligned sentence/document pairs across languages.
types.where_useful: Only if the project targets multilingual specialists; otherwise minor (cross-lingual retrieval, the ling specialist).
types.edge_over_others: Unlocks non-English coverage cheaply — but Phase A is English-first, so the payoff is conditional.
types.rationale: Low unless multilingual is an explicit goal; parked for a later phase.

types.what_it_is: Massive deduplicated web/text corpora (billions–trillions of tokens) for base-model pretraining.
types.where_useful: We fine-tune existing base models, so raw corpora matter only for *continued pretraining* to domain-adapt a vertical before SFT.
types.edge_over_others: Unmatched scale and breadth — but mostly redundant with what our base models already absorbed; expensive to use for fine-tuning gains.
types.rationale: High prestige, low marginal value for a fine-tuning project — useful only as a domain-adaptation pre-step, not for specialist behavior.

types.type: Non-text & multimodal modalities (image · audio · video · 3D · geospatial · tabular · timeseries · document · robotics/RL)
types.what_it_is: Everything outside plain text: vision (image/VQA/OCR-document), speech (ASR/TTS), video, 3D/geospatial, tabular/time-series, and robotics/RL trajectories. These are HF's literal `modality` tags.
types.where_useful: Not in Phase A (text specialists). Relevant to future multimodal phases: document/OCR for ingesting PDFs into KBs (biblio/libarch), tabular/timeseries for markets/money quant signals, image/design assets for the design/maker/creator specialists.
types.edge_over_others: Each unlocks a sense our text-only system lacks — but adds modality-specific model machinery the current architecture doesn't have.
types.rationale: Out-of-scope for the current text-reasoning fleet; flagged so the roadmap can pull specific slices (esp. document/OCR + tabular) when multimodal phases open.
